LXV Wine: A Sensory Wine Experience in Paso Robles

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 10:46
Instaread
  • November 9, 2026
  • By Paso Wine Collective

Most tasting rooms in Paso Robles pour wine. LXV Wine does something different: they pair each glass with a hand-blended spice served over local sheep’s milk cheese, then ask you to taste the wine again. The tannins shift. The aromatics lift. A Syrah you thought you knew becomes something else entirely. It’s a format nobody else in Paso Robles has replicated, and it’s what makes LXV Wine Paso Robles visitors talk about long after they’ve driven home.

Founded in 2010 by Neeta and Kunal Mittal, LXV takes its name from the Roman numeral 65 — a reference to the 64 sutras that structure classical Indian art, music, and hospitality. The Mittals consider the moment of connection between host and guest the 65th, and they’ve built every part of this winery around that idea, from the unhurried seated tastings to the spice blends they develop in-house.

  1. The Wines: Three Labels, One House
  2. The Estate Behind the Wines
  3. Visiting LXV Wine in Downtown Paso Robles
  4. Wine Club Memberships
  5. Plan Your Visit to LXV Wine
  6. Frequently Asked Questions About LXV Wine

What Makes LXV Different

The signature experience at LXV is the Classic Wine & Spice Tasting. You’re seated — not standing at a bar — and a host guides you through four wines at a pace that lets you actually pay attention. Each wine is poured alongside a custom spice blend on sheep’s milk cheese sourced from a local creamery.

You taste the wine on its own first. Then you try the spice pairing. The difference isn’t subtle. Spice compounds interact with tannin and fruit in ways that change the wine’s texture and aroma, and the guided format gives you the vocabulary to understand what’s happening in the glass rather than just noticing that something shifted.

The whole experience runs about 90 minutes, which is longer than a standard Paso tasting. That’s intentional. LXV’s hosts work with one or two groups at a time, and nobody rushes you through. If you’ve done enough five-minute pours to last a lifetime, this is the antidote.

Classic Wine & Spice Tasting: $35 for the wine flight, plus $15 for the spice pairing add-on. The tasting fee is waived with a three-bottle purchase. The spice pairing is optional, but it’s the reason to come — don’t skip it. More information.

LXV’s Other Tasting Experiences

The spice pairing is the entry point, but LXV offers several ways to go deeper, depending on how much time you have and what you’re drawn to.

A Study in Cabernet Franc: At $45 ($35 for club members), this focused flight walks you through four expressions of Cabernet Franc: Blanc de Franc (a white wine made from a red grape — worth trying for the novelty alone), The Tempo Reserve, the G2 North single-vineyard bottling, and the MESO Cabernet Franc. Decanter awarded the 2023 MESO Cabernet Franc Best Red Wine of the Vintage for Paso Robles and scored it 95 points, so this isn’t a casual lineup.

The MESO Collection: For $65 ($45 for members), you taste four single-vineyard MESO wines poured ahead of time so they’ve had a chance to open up. The current lineup includes the 2022 Cabernet Sauvignon from Gateway Vineyard, 2022 Syrah from the estate Armaa.N Vineyard, 2023 Cabernet Franc from G2 North, and 2023 Sangiovese from Armaa.N. The fee is waived with a two-bottle purchase.

Vineyard & Table at Armaa.N Estate: This is the experience for visitors who want to see where the wine actually comes from. At $75 ($60 for club members), you get a guided walk through the 13.5-acre Armaa.N Vineyard in the Willow Creek District, followed by a seated tasting of the 2022 Maison Mittal wines and a conversation about terroir, blend decisions, and farming practices. It runs by appointment on seasonal dates for small groups only, and either the owners or winemaker Jeff Strekas typically hosts.

The Wines: Three Labels, One House

LXV operates under what the Mittals call The House of Mittal — three distinct labels, each with a different purpose and price point.

LXV is the original label and the one most visitors encounter first. The wines are Bordeaux-inspired blends and single varietals grown at the estate and select Central Coast vineyards. The LXV Reserve Syrah from Bien Nacido Vineyard earned 99 points from Jeb Dunnuck — the highest score any wine in the portfolio has received. Other recent standouts include The Secret (a Bordeaux-style red blend) and The Tempo Reserve Cabernet Franc.

MESO by LXV is the single-vineyard collection. Each wine is sourced from one site — Armaa.N Estate, Gateway Vineyard, G2 North, or Bien Nacido — and released under the vineyard’s name. The 2022 MESO Sangiovese from Armaa.N earned a spot on Wine Enthusiast’s Top 100 Cellar Selections for 2025, and the 2022 MESO Armaa.N Syrah scored 96 points from the same publication.

Maison Mittal is the collector tier. Production is capped under 1,000 cases per year, and the wines draw from both Paso Robles and Saint-Émilion, where the Mittals work with Bordeaux consultant Frédéric Ammons and winemaker Lionel Kreff at Château Le Chatelet, a Grand Cru Classé estate. The 2022 Maison Mittal G2 North Cabernet Franc–Cabernet Sauvignon earned 97 points from Wine Enthusiast and was named to their Top 100 Cellar Selections for 2026, alongside a 98-point score from The SOMM Journal. Bottles start around $175.

Between the three labels, LXV has earned 99 points from Jeb Dunnuck, 97 from Wine Enthusiast and Forbes, 98 from The SOMM Journal, and 95 from Decanter — scores that put the winery in rare company for a tasting room of this size. Neeta and Kunal Mittal were also named Wine Enthusiast Future 40 Tastemakers, a recognition of both the wine quality and the pairing concept they’ve pioneered.

The Estate Behind the Wines

The 13.5-acre Armaa.N Vineyard sits in Paso Robles’ Willow Creek District, one of the cooler sub-AVAs on the west side. The property includes a 50-year-old pine forest and lavender planted alongside the vines — details you’ll notice if you visit for the Vineyard & Table experience.

The Mittals farm without synthetic pesticides, herbicides, or fertilizers, relying on winter cover crops and compost tea to build soil health. The estate is working toward CCOF organic certification, with USDA and CDFA recognition of their farming practices already in place. Winemaker Jeff Strekas manages the vineyard alongside the cellar work, and the low yields — a deliberate choice — concentrate flavor in ways the scores reflect.

Armaa.N also includes Cabernet Sauvignon planted with To Kalon clone material, used for limited-production magnums under the Maison Mittal label. A dedicated estate winery and tasting room is planned for the vineyard property by 2028, which will add a second location to LXV’s current downtown presence.

Visiting LXV Wine in Downtown Paso Robles

LXV’s tasting room sits at 1306-B Pine Street, a short walk from Downtown City Park and within easy reach of the downtown Paso Robles wine tasting district. The space is small and intentionally intimate — there are no crowds, no background noise from a busy bar, and no pressure to buy and move on.

Hours: Wednesday through Monday, 10 AM to 5 PM. Closed Tuesdays.

Reservations: Book through Tock. Walk-ins are welcome based on availability, but the seated format means tables fill, and advance booking is the safer bet — especially on weekends.

Group size: Tables accommodate up to six guests. Parties of seven or more should email the winery to arrange a private tasting.

Same-day visits: Call (805) 296-1902 to check what’s open.

Owner pours: Neeta and Kunal Mittal often host tastings themselves. If meeting a winery’s founders matters to you, email ahead to ask when they’ll be in the room.

LXV pairs naturally with a food-and-wine focused Paso Robles itinerary. The spice pairing is enough of a culinary experience to anchor a tasting day that includes lunch at one of the restaurants in downtown Paso Robles, and the 90-minute format means you’ll want to plan around it rather than squeeze it between two other stops. Two or three other tastings in the same day is realistic; five is not, if LXV is one of them.

Wine Club Memberships

LXV runs two club tiers, both shipping twice a year with seasonal spice pairings and recipes included alongside the wines.

Maya ($325 per shipment, 4 bottles) includes 15% off all LXV wines and 2 complimentary tastings per quarter — which means you can bring guests back without paying the tasting fee each time. Kama ($550 per shipment, 8 bottles) steps up to 25% off and 4 complimentary tastings per quarter. LXV covers roughly half the shipping cost on both tiers.

For visitors who fall for the spice pairing format and want to recreate it at home, the club shipments include the spice blends designed for each wine in the box. It’s one of the few wine clubs that ships a complete experience rather than just bottles.

Plan Your Visit to LXV Wine

LXV isn’t a drop-in-and-sip kind of stop, and that’s precisely the point. The seated, guided format and the wine-and-spice concept offer something you genuinely can’t find at any other winery in Paso Robles, and the critical scores — from Jeb Dunnuck to Wine Enthusiast to Decanter — back up what the palate already tells you.

Book a Classic Wine & Spice Tasting on Tock, plan for 90 minutes, and don’t skip the spice add-on. If you’re ready for a deeper dive, the MESO Collection or the Vineyard & Table experience at Armaa.N are worth the upgrade.

Check the LXV Wine website for current hours and any seasonal schedule changes before your visit. For more wineries in Paso Robles worth building a trip around, explore our full directory.

Frequently Asked Questions About LXV Wine

Do I need a reservation to visit LXV Wine?

Reservations through Tock are strongly recommended. Walk-ins are accepted based on availability, but because every tasting is seated and guided, tables fill — particularly on weekends and holidays. Booking ahead guarantees your spot.

How much does a wine tasting at LXV cost?

The Classic Wine & Spice Tasting is $35, with the spice pairing add-on at $15. The Cabernet Franc flight is $45, and the MESO Collection tasting is $65. Tasting fees on the Classic and MESO experiences are waived with a qualifying wine purchase. Club members receive complimentary tastings each quarter.

Is LXV Wine kid-friendly or dog-friendly?

LXV’s intimate, seated format is designed for adults. Contact the winery directly at (805) 296-1902 to ask about their current policies for children and pets before your visit.

Can I buy LXV wines online?

Yes. LXV ships wine to consumers in most U.S. states through their online shop at lxvwine.com. The Perfumed Garden at-home pairing kit ($95, serves two) is also available for shipping — it includes three wines, three spice blends, and on-demand video tastings hosted by Neeta Mittal.
